status: Conjugate kinematic study; production rotor dimensions and hydraulic performance unverified

primary_research.title: Profile Design and Numerical Calculation of Instantaneous Flow Rate of a Gerotor Pump
primary_research.authors: Hao Liu, Jae-Cheon Lee, Alex Yoon, Sang-Tae Kim
primary_research.applicable_sections: 2.1–2.2, especially circular-cutter family and inward equidistant envelope; circular-arc outer teeth
primary_research.scope: Mathematical construction only. The paper is not a Ford application or production geometry reference. Its hydraulic calculations are not implemented here.

construction.inner_curve: C(t)=(26cos(t)-3.5cos(5t),26sin(t)-3.5sin(5t)); inward unit normal=(-Cy',Cx')/|C'|; profile=C+8.025*normal. 720 samples interpolated by periodic spline.
construction.outer_cavity: Radius26.5 root circle with five radius8 circular teeth whose centers are radius26 at72deg intervals.
construction.conjugacy: In the inner rotor frame an outer tooth center follows C(t), with t=-inner_angle/5. Envelope normals meet the corresponding circular cutter, so equal-direction4:5 angular velocity preserves conjugate geometry, offset by the deliberate normal gap.

motion.axis: Local Z after existing20deg group tilt
motion.retainer: Co-rotates with intermediate shaft because its existing bore is hexagonal; grip and axial retention mechanics remain provisional.
motion.continuous_socket_fit: All three coaxial shafts use the same angular motion; relative hex phase and10mm upper/9mm lower axial insertion are invariant for every angle.
motion.lower_coupling: Provisional D-flat: shaft radius4.75 and flatX3.7; inner bore radius4.78 and flatX3.73. Flat extends shaft-localZ-21..4 covering entire rotor engagement. Clearance fit does not model loaded face deflection/contact.

limitations: Four/five tooth count comes from the earlier interpretation of the inspection illustration, not a dimensioned manufacturing print.
Every rotor radius, normal gap, axial dimension, shaft-flat dimension and tilt is provisional.
Periodic spline approximates the analytic envelope; sampled interference and gap checks do not certify manufacturing tolerances.
Existing crossed-helical cam gears retain their prior source and dimensional caveats; repeating their motion check does not validate production tooth design.
No oil pressure, flow rate, sealing, cavitation, port timing, strength or serviceability certification is claimed.
